Israel invaded Lebanon that summer and we were diverted off the coast of Beirut, where we stayed underway for weeks, without port calls or a break, while we evacuated U.S. citizens. John won 288 games during a career that stretched from 1963 to 1989 — the second-most by any pitcher of the modern era who has not been elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame. A Harvard professor is facing criticism for using AI to condense a longer iteration of an opinion piece written for the Financial Times (FT) on Thursday. "Trump is taxing the dark matter that pays America’s way," read the headline of the piece by Harvard professor Ricardo Hausmann. The piece was published by the FT on August 13. "It has come to our attention that AI was used to condense a longer draft of this column prior to submission to the FT and our own editorial involvement. The FT editorial code of conduct specifically prohibits the use of AI in the writing process," an editor's note at the top of Hausmann's piece says. The FT told Fox News Digital the publication was going to conduct an "editorial review process to look at this piece in more detail," but otherwise pointed to the editor's note. item.title: War on Iran: Phase II, Day 37
item.description:
Abu Dhabi is not the Gulf’s biggest energy exporter, but ADNOC has emerged as one of its most flexible — thanks to geography, defense capabilities, and a willingness to take risks. The state oil company has led the region in ramping up oil output during the Iran war, helped by the UAE’s exit from oil cartel OPEC in May: The UAE exported around 3.8 million barrels a day in June. Abu Dhabi is expanding a pipeline to Fujairah that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, while some of its tankers are managing to slip through the waterway, helping ADNOC maintain and sometimes even exceed prewar flows. Its vessels have also carried Iraqi crude, adding to the cushion for global oil markets. The human cost has, however, been high : 23 of its ships have been attacked by Iran, killing one crew member and injuring about 20 others. — Mohammed Sergie

item.title: Even College Students Have Stopped Hanging Out
item.description:
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. If anyone were to be immune to America’s loneliness epidemic, it would be college students. For years, Americans have been going to fewer parties and spending more time alone. But college has historically been about socializing—or, let’s just say it, partying—as much as it has been about education. It’s where young people escape parental supervision, move in with roommates, and encounter thousands of potential new friends. But the antisocial century has arrived on campus. Today’s students spend much less time socializing than past generations did. In 1994, 32 percent of college seniors spent more than six hours a week partying. More than 70,000 migrants, mainly from Morocco, swam and scaled border fences to reach Ceuta, which is situated on the African continent, in a matter of days last month. Most of the illegal border crossers have since returned to Africa after complaining about a lack of food and shelter in Ceuta. Between 5,000 and 8,000 migrants remain in Ceuta, according to Reuters. Most of the migrants said they left Africa to find work, which typically does not qualify as an asylum claim.
